title: The Pricing Curve: Why Email SaaS Gets Expensive Exactly When You Succeed
author: Juan Rodriguez
excerpt: Per-subscriber pricing means your bill grows with your list, not your usage. How to compute your own crossover point - and what a flat-cost stack changes.
content:
Email platforms charge by the subscriber. That sounds fair until you plot it: your list is the one metric you want to grow, and every unit of growth raises the rent. The faster you succeed, the faster the bill climbs.

The shape of the curve

SaaS email pricing is a staircase of tiers keyed to list size. The steps arrive at the worst moments - right after a campaign works, right after a launch brings in subscribers. And the list keeps costing money even when you do not send: inactive subscribers count toward the tier on most platforms.

Compute your own crossover

Take your current monthly platform bill, project it at two and five times your list size using the vendor's public tiers, and compare against the cost of a server plus an hour a month of maintenance. The numbers differ per business, but the direction rarely does: the curve only bends one way.

What the flat-cost stack looks like

Self-hosted email flips the shape: software you control, a server at a fixed monthly price, sending costs that track actual volume through your MTA or relay. List growth becomes pure upside - the tenth thousand subscribers cost the same as the first.

The non-money part

Per-subscriber pricing also distorts behavior: teams prune engaged-but-quiet subscribers to stay under a tier, and hoard old addresses to avoid shrinking. Neither is good marketing. When the list stops being the billing unit, list hygiene becomes a deliverability decision instead of a financial one.
